This is a sample mathematical post. It is mainly used to test display math, theorem environments, and proof blocks.

Let $\Sigma^2 \subset M^3$ be a closed two-sided surface with unit normal $\nu$. If the variation vector field is $X=f\nu$, then the first variation of area is

$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_t)
= -\int_\Sigma H f \, d\mu .
$$ {#eq-first-variation}

::: {#thm-minimal-critical}
## Minimal surfaces as critical points

A closed two-sided surface $\Sigma \subset M$ is minimal if and only if it is a critical point of the area functional under all compactly supported normal variations.
:::

::: {.proof}
By @eq-first-variation, the first variation vanishes for every smooth function $f$ if and only if

$$
\int_\Sigma H f\,d\mu = 0
$$

for all $f$. This is equivalent to $H=0$ on $\Sigma$.
:::

The statement above is @thm-minimal-critical. In future posts, this style can be used for lemmas, propositions, definitions, remarks, and equations.

::: {#rem-writing-style}
## Writing style

For a research note, I usually want three layers: the formal statement, the geometric meaning, and the proof mechanism.
:::
